records.title: OpenAI Codex
records.description: A general-purpose coding agent for reading, editing, running commands, and reviewing code in a local repository.

blocks.value: A general-purpose coding agent for reading, editing, running commands, and reviewing code in a local repository.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Useful as the main code execution loop for a game project: break down gameplay, maintain scripts, run builds, and inspect failures. Engine integration still requires a CLI, editor bridge, or MCP server; compiling successfully does not establish that a game is playable.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: Official OpenAI coding agent and OpenAI-authored workflow. Use the OpenAI brand mark, not a generated substitute.

records.title: Claude Code
records.description: A coding agent that reads and edits projects, runs tools, and supports skills, hooks, and MCP through terminal and IDE interfaces.

blocks.value: A coding agent that reads and edits projects, runs tools, and supports skills, hooks, and MCP through terminal and IDE interfaces.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Can develop game scripts, migrate architecture, troubleshoot builds, and connect to Unity, Godot, or UE through community MCP servers. Use CLAUDE.md, skills, and editor state together; one MCP demonstration does not establish complete engine automation.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: Official Anthropic product and SDK. The organization avatar is an official corporate mark.

records.title: Gemini CLI
records.description: Google's open-source terminal coding agent with file access, shell tools, extensions, and MCP support.

blocks.value: Google's open-source terminal coding agent with file access, shell tools, extensions, and MCP support.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Can help understand game projects, edit scripts, and drive editors through MCP. The official README states that Antigravity CLI replaced Gemini CLI for unpaid-tier and Google One users on June 18, 2026, and that Gemini CLI is not optimized for the latest Gemini models. Check the account-specific migration guidance before choosing this entry point.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: Official Google Gemini project organization; the Gemini mark represents the product brand.

records.title: DeepSeek · Agent Integrations
records.description: Official guidance for using DeepSeek as a model backend within agent harnesses such as Claude Code.

blocks.value: Official guidance for using DeepSeek as a model backend within agent harnesses such as Claude Code.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: The Anthropic API compatibility layer connects DeepSeek to existing tool loops. The harness handles files, tests, and engine connections. The guide supports ordinary tool calls but ignores the server-side mcp_servers field and does not support MCP-specific content blocks. Client-side MCP tools therefore remain the harness's responsibility; API compatibility does not establish complete feature parity.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: Official DeepSeek organization links its API documentation. This entry covers a model integration guide, not a separate game agent.

records.title: OpenCode
records.description: An open-source coding agent with multiple model providers, Plan / Build modes, and project instructions.

blocks.value: An open-source coding agent with multiple model providers, Plan / Build modes, and project instructions.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Useful for planning and editing game projects with independently selected providers and models. Pin V1 or V2: the V2 migration guide documents incompatible plugin/server APIs, external-directory access allowed by default, and no running LSP or LSP diagnostics despite accepted configuration. Validate permissions, MCP integrations, and compiler/test feedback for the chosen version; editor and gameplay inspection still require separate tools.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: Exact OpenCode logo referenced by the official README; use an appropriate light/dark variant without redrawing it.

blocks.value: Exact Cline project icon referenced at the top of the official README.

records.title: Aider
records.description: A terminal AI pair-programming tool built around repository maps, Git changes, and lint and test feedback.

blocks.value: A terminal AI pair-programming tool built around repository maps, Git changes, and lint and test feedback.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: Exact logo linked by the official project README.

blocks.value: An open-source development console for managing local, remote, and cloud agent environments.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Can centralize multi-agent tasks, environments, and execution records for game projects. Pin client/server versions rather than assuming interface parity. Game-specific tools and acceptance checks still need to be supplied.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: Official OpenHands README logo; the Software Agent SDK is maintained in the same OpenHands organization.

blocks.value: Runs the Claude Code binary and tool loop inside a process you operate, with Python or TypeScript APIs for permissions, sessions, hooks, and MCP. It can support game-specific repair and validation services, but domain tools, scoring rules, and runtime environments must be supplied. This differs from a Client SDK for direct model calls; the official overview also specifies Anthropic Commercial Terms and separate authentication constraints.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: Official Anthropic product and SDK. The organization avatar is an official corporate mark.

records.title: mini-swe-agent
records.description: A minimal shell-based coding-agent research baseline designed for modification and trace inspection.

blocks.value: A minimal shell-based coding-agent research baseline designed for modification and trace inspection.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Useful for isolating model, prompt, and environment effects in game code generation and repair, or wrapping headless engine commands. Its minimal loop executes commands in independent subprocesses rather than a persistent shell, so working-directory and environment setup must be carried into each command or script. It is a general software-engineering baseline; playability, visuals, and physics require additional validation.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: The official MkDocs configuration explicitly sets assets/mini_square.svg as both logo and favicon. Prefer the actual project mark over assigning one university from a multi-institution team.

records.description: An open Markdown format for giving coding agents build commands, test rules, and project conventions.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here

blocks.value: The official format website states Agent Skills was originally developed by Anthropic. Label as creator; the open format is adopted across the ecosystem.

records.description: OpenAI's browser game workflow covering planning, project instructions, asset generation, and browser iteration.

blocks.value: OpenAI's browser game workflow covering planning, project instructions, asset generation, and browser iteration.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution

records.title: MCP for Unity
records.description: A community MCP bridge connecting general-purpose coding agents to the Unity Editor.

blocks.value: A community MCP bridge connecting general-purpose coding agents to the Unity Editor.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Exposes editor operations for scenes, GameObjects, C# scripts, assets, and tests. The checked installation source declares Unity 2021.3 LTS or newer, plus Python 3.10+ and uv. These are declared requirements, not versions tested here. The project is independent of Unity Technologies; pin bridge/editor versions and validate compilation, screenshots, and PlayMode tests.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: Exact MCP for Unity project logo from its README. Independent community integration, explicitly not affiliated with Unity Technologies. The operator guide belongs to the same repository.

records.title: Unity-MCP Operator Guide
records.description: A practical MCP for Unity skill: inspect editor state, act, wait for compilation and domain reload, then verify results.

blocks.value: A practical MCP for Unity skill: inspect editor state, act, wait for compilation and domain reload, then verify results.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Defines resource-first scene operations and requires checking compilation, domain reload, tool readiness, and blocking reasons before further edits. Script changes are followed by console and screenshot checks. This is a procedure source for MCP for Unity, not an installed or tested integration here; examples and parameters depend on bridge, Unity, UI, and input-system versions.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: Exact MCP for Unity project logo from its README. Independent community integration, explicitly not affiliated with Unity Technologies. The operator guide belongs to the same repository.

records.title: Godot MCP · Coding-Solo
records.description: A community MCP server for launching Godot, running projects, reading logs, and performing basic scene operations.

blocks.value: A community MCP server for launching Godot, running projects, reading logs, and performing basic scene operations.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Supports project execution, debug output capture, scene and node creation, Sprite2D texture loading, and some 3D MeshLibrary operations. It can give agents feedback from real projects; these interfaces do not provide complete visual playtesting or every editor feature. At the checked commit, the server keeps one active project process and sends kill before spawning another without awaiting prior exit. Stop returns after sending a kill request rather than waiting for process exit; natural exit clears the handle used by get_debug_output. Archive output separately for reliable crash evidence.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: ownership is confirmed by the repository and creator profile, but no independent project graphic logo was found. The README has Godot ASCII art only. Do not use a default identicon, a personal photograph, or the Godot engine logo as creator branding.

records.title: MCP for Blender
records.description: A Blender add-on and MCP server for agent-driven modeling, materials, Python execution, and visual feedback.

blocks.value: A Blender add-on and MCP server for agent-driven modeling, materials, Python execution, and visual feedback.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Useful for 3D game assets and scene prototypes with viewport feedback. Formerly blender-mcp, this community bridge can execute arbitrary Python inside Blender; use trusted tasks and saved copies. The checked documentation distinguishes default minimal usage telemetry from opt-in creative-content collection; DISABLE_TELEMETRY=true disables both. Review the opt-in data terms before enabling content capture. Validate topology, scale, UVs, collision, and exports separately.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: repository and linked project site confirm an independent community integration, explicitly not affiliated with Blender Foundation. No separate project or organization logo has been confirmed; do not replace it with the official Blender logo or a personal portrait.

records.title: Unreal MCP · chongdashu
records.description: A Python MCP server and UE C++ plugin connecting agents to Actors, Blueprints, and viewport controls.

blocks.value: A Python MCP server and UE C++ plugin connecting agents to Actors, Blueprints, and viewport controls.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Covers Actor transforms, Blueprint classes and components, some node graphs, and editor camera operations. The README declares Unreal Engine 5.5+ and Python 3.12+ and supplies a UE5.5 example; later-version compatibility is not independently tested here. The author marks it experimental and advises against production use. Pin versions and verify supported operations individually.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: repository ownership is chongdashu; the linked creator profile identifies AI Oriented Dev and aioriented.dev. No project/creator brand image has been confirmed. Do not use Epic/Unreal branding as an implied creator.

records.title: Playwright MCP
records.description: Microsoft's browser automation MCP server for exposing page structure, interactions, and browser feedback to agents.

blocks.value: Microsoft's browser automation MCP server for exposing page structure, interactions, and browser feedback to agents.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Useful for browser game menus, HUDs, launch flows, keyboard input, and screenshots. The default interface uses accessibility trees; coordinate-based mouse tools require the optional vision capability. Neither interface automatically exposes internal Canvas or WebGL state, so game debug instrumentation may be needed. The checked README warns that the server is not a security boundary and documents browser_run_code_unsafe as arbitrary JavaScript execution in the Playwright server process. The separate Playwright CLI repository provides a CLI + Skills workflow.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: Official Microsoft Playwright project. Use the real Playwright brand mark; it is a Microsoft-maintained MCP, unlike third-party engine bridges.

records.title: Godot · Command Line Tutorial
records.description: Godot's official CLI reference for headless operation, script checks, asset import, execution, and export.

blocks.value: Godot's official CLI reference for headless operation, script checks, asset import, execution, and export.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Lets coding agents launch projects, read logs, parse scripts, and export builds through commands, reducing GUI dependence. The --check-only flag parses a script supplied with --script; it does not execute gameplay tests. Supported flags vary by build type, and unknown flags are silently ignored; check the selected binary's --help. Headless runs cannot replace real rendering and input tests.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: Official engine and its own documentation/demo repositories. The official Godot organization avatar is its recognizable project logo.

The repository states that master targets the development engine; choose a matching branch for a stable release to avoid mistaking version conflicts for generation failures.

blocks.value: Official engine and its own documentation/demo repositories. The official Godot organization avatar is its recognizable project logo.

blocks.value: A community Godot testing framework for GDScript assertions, test doubles, and parameterized cases.

records.title: GDQuest · First 2D Game
records.description: A GDQuest tutorial for a Godot 2D survival game, with complete scripts, a project, and troubleshooting notes.

blocks.value: A GDQuest tutorial for a Godot 2D survival game, with complete scripts, a project, and troubleshooting notes.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Covers movement, aiming, projectiles, enemy spawning, and failure states as a reference for a complete core loop. The tutorial was made with Godot 4.1 and updated to 4.6. Its troubleshooting explains grounded / floating modes and an enemy count limit. Code uses MIT while art assets use CC BY-NC-SA 4.0; check reuse conditions separately.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: GDQuest-authored course and library page; use GDQuest's own organization mark rather than Godot branding.

records.title: Unity · Manual
records.description: Official Unity documentation for projects, the editor, scripting, rendering, physics, asset import, and publishing.

blocks.value: Official Unity documentation for projects, the editor, scripting, rendering, physics, asset import, and publishing.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Provides agents with concrete C# and editor project constraints, plus 2D and 3D workflows and versioned package references. Pin the Editor, render pipeline, and Package Manager versions together; the Unity name alone does not establish API or material compatibility.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: Official Unity editor documentation, test framework, and demos. This association is limited to official Unity resources, not third-party MCP projects.

records.title: Unity Test Framework
records.description: Unity's official testing framework, with Edit mode, Play mode, and command-line execution.

blocks.value: Unity's official testing framework, with Edit mode, Play mode, and command-line execution.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Enables ongoing regression checks for generated scripts and scene behavior, using UnityTest across frames to check lifecycles, coroutines, and state changes. Edit mode and Play mode have different execution loops; tests should wait for real frames or conditions rather than only confirming script creation. The separately checked Test Framework 1.4.6 API returns a job GUID and documents multi-frame cancellation cleanup. Active tests become Canceled and remaining tests NotRun; do not equate cancellation with passing or assume compatibility with every Editor package version.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: Official Unity editor documentation, test framework, and demos. This association is limited to official Unity resources, not third-party MCP projects.

records.title: Unity · 2D Tech Demos

blocks.value: Official Unity 2D example source for Tilemaps, Scripted Tiles, brushes, and runtime map changes.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Offers source scenes for tile collision lookup, destructible maps, and palette switching. The inspected project records Unity 6000.3.3f1, URP 17.3.0, and Input System 1.17.0, while the README says 2021.1 onward. Its manifest selects 2d-extras' package_6000.3 Git branch but the committed lockfile records registry 6.0.1; resolve and pin dependencies before testing. Source review did not establish import, playback, or compatibility across Editor versions.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: Official Unity editor documentation, test framework, and demos. This association is limited to official Unity resources, not third-party MCP projects.

blocks.value: Jasper Flick's Unity movement tutorial explains character control through slopes, steps, and contact timing.

blocks.value: The author uses test scenes to reproduce loss of ground contact, ghost collisions, raycasts, and ground snapping, giving agents causal explanations of physics behavior. blocks.label: Identity & attribution

blocks.value: Official Epic documentation for UE C++, Blueprints, rendering, animation, physics, and packaging.

records.title: Unreal · Automation Test Framework
records.description: UE's official infrastructure for unit, functional, content stress, and screenshot comparison tests.

blocks.value: UE's official infrastructure for unit, functional, content stress, and screenshot comparison tests.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Can bring Blueprint compilation, level loading, simulated input, and visual regression checks into an agent feedback loop, alongside interfaces such as Functional Testing. Tests require the appropriate plugins and state cleanup; the framework runs within the engine. Preserve the report and distinguish compatible editor and client test contexts.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution

blocks.label: Why it belongs here

The current README targets Phaser 4, and the labs site defaults to its latest development build; select and pin the version matching your project. The MIT license covers example code, not bundled art assets. Review asset permissions before reuse and test in a real browser.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: Official framework and examples organization. README explicitly attributes Phaser logo and characters to Phaser Studio Inc. The organization avatar avoids using a version-4 wordmark on Phaser-3 examples.

records.title: Unreal Engine · Remote Control API
records.description: Exposes reflected editor properties and functions over HTTP for external tooling.

blocks.value: Exposes reflected editor properties and functions over HTTP for external tooling.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Remote Control provides a native engine integration surface distinct from a community MCP bridge. Property writes can request editor transactions and change notifications, but an acknowledged mutation does not establish package-save completion. The rolling Epic guide labels this feature Beta and disables it by default in packaged builds and -game. Enable the appropriate plugin, restrict network exposure, and qualify editor versus packaged-runtime access separately.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: Official documentation identifies the publisher of this interface. The existing bundled mark identifies the same publisher; documented API availability does not establish a working GameMap adapter.

records.title: Unity · Addressables Build and Loading APIs
records.description: Builds addressable content from explicit profiles and loads assets through asynchronous handles.

blocks.value: Unity · Addressables Build and Loading APIs
Builds addressable content from explicit profiles and loads assets through asynchronous handles.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: The checked Addressables 1.21 documentation separates content builds from executable builds. Build settings, active profile, builder, and content-state file affect outputs. Runtime loading returns a handle whose status and result must be checked and later released. A key matching several assets can select only the first; preserve dependency and cache provenance.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: Official documentation identifies the publisher of this interface. The existing bundled mark identifies the same publisher; documented API availability does not establish a working GameMap adapter.

records.title: GameGPT
records.description: Studies automated game development through multi-agent planning and code generation.

blocks.value: Studies automated game development through multi-agent planning and code generation.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Planning, review, and implementation agents break down game requirements and generate code, with a focus on hallucination and redundancy. This is an early research framework for game development agents. The linked repository contains only the paper and README; it is not a verified, ready-to-deploy product.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: The paper lists first author Dake Chen at AutoGame Research and uses autogame.ai email addresses for other AutoGame authors. The logo is linked by AutoGame's official homepage. Other author affiliations include X-Institute, USC, and Tsinghua; this is a representative research affiliation, not exclusive ownership or endorsement.

records.title: OpenGame
records.description: Generates browser game projects with reusable templates and debugging skills.

blocks.value: Generates browser game projects with reusable templates and debugging skills.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Turns natural-language requirements into web projects using Template Skill and Debug Skill for Canvas, Phaser, three.js, and other templates. The public CLI accepts OpenAI-compatible model endpoints; the paper also introduces GameCoder-27B. Browser execution and visual judging assess build health, usability, and intent alignment. The README still lists the standalone evaluation pipeline as forthcoming; model weights and full evaluation reproducibility are not established by the framework release alone.

records.description: Evaluates coding agents on development tasks in existing Godot projects.

blocks.value: Evaluates coding agents on development tasks in existing Godot projects.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: The repository contains 333 tasks across 2D, 3D, UI, and gameplay logic. Agents receive an existing project and a task, then produce changes that can be checked in the engine. Comparable official runs require Godot 4.4.1 and provide image or video feedback. This measures bounded development tasks, not the quality of commercial games created from scratch.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: The paper lists first author Wayne Chi and most coauthors at Carnegie Mellon; one coauthor is at Princeton. This represents the first author's affiliation, not a claim of exclusive authorship. The 900px square logo is the image displayed on CMU's official brand standards University Logo page.

blocks.value: Benchmarks game creation, bug fixing, and iterative improvement in three tracks.

blocks.value: The paper introduces GameGen, GameFix, and GameOpt using complete development trajectories to study the lifecycle beyond a single generation. At review, the official repository still said data and evaluation code were being prepared for release. Treat it as a paper and protocol reference, not a ready-to-run benchmark.

Import and visual acceptance checks remain necessary.

records.title: GameEngineBench
records.description: Tests agent-written C++ runtime changes in real Unreal Engine projects.

blocks.value: Tests agent-written C++ runtime changes in real Unreal Engine projects.

After compilation and Play-in-Editor listen-server tests, an LLM judge reviews the specification, test evidence, edits, and reference solution to determine success. The paper-linked repository could not be retrieved during review, so runnable-code availability remains unverified. The scope is local C++ implementation, not complete 3D game generation.

blocks.value: A community MCP bridge for querying, editing, and testing Unity projects.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Exposes scenes, GameObjects, components, Prefabs, logs, Unity Test Runner, and other editor operations to MCP clients. This community tool is separate from Unity's official plugin. Its README warns that entering Play Mode with domain reload can disconnect the bridge; check the installed version, test configuration, and actual results. Editor automation alone does not establish correct gameplay.

It can provide controllable scenes and data for AI development workflows; real-time games still need optimization, collision, and gameplay integration.

records.title: Video2Game
records.description: Reconstructs real-world video into interactive 3D environments for the browser.

blocks.value: Reconstructs real-world video into interactive 3D environments for the browser.

blocks.value: Compositional World Modeling with Products of Programmatic Experts combines LLM-synthesized programs in an exponentially weighted product of experts, learning complex stochastic world models from few observations. The paper connects these models to planners in Pong and Montezuma's Revenge to demonstrate sample efficiency and generalization to new levels. This is programmatic dynamics modeling rather than an art generation tool.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: The original paper lists Cornell University, University of Cambridge, The Alan Turing Institute, and Dalhousie University. Select Cornell, the first listed institution and the first-author institution. The SVG is the official Cornell CS homepage identity, also used for WorldCoder.

records.title: FactorSim
records.description: Generates simulation and task code from language using factorized state representations.

blocks.value: Generates simulation and task code from language using factorized state representations.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Generative Simulation via Factorized Representation uses a factorized POMDP representation to reduce context per generation step. It generates 2D game simulations for agent training. Its robotics experiments generate task code, including object states and reward structure, within the existing CLIPort framework. The game benchmark covers eight Pygame environments; 3D game generation is future work in the NeurIPS 2024 paper. Robotics experiments retain 3D relevance without establishing generation of a complete physics engine.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: The project page assigns the first author Fan-Yun Sun and most authors to Stanford University; NVIDIA is the second institution. The logo is an official Stanford touch icon linked by https://identity.stanford.edu/.

records.title: Genie: Generative Interactive Environments
records.description: Learns latent-action-controlled 2D worlds from videos without action labels.

blocks.value: Learns latent-action-controlled 2D worlds from videos without action labels.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Combines a spatiotemporal video tokenizer, autoregressive dynamics, and a latent action model into generative interactive environments. Users can begin with an image or sketch and explore frame by frame. The ICML 2024 contribution centers on learning control without ground-truth action labels. Dynamics remain implicit in the model, without editable or queryable game rule programs.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: The original paper explicitly identifies the authors with Google DeepMind. Jeff Clune additionally lists the University of British Columbia. Select the main institution; use the official google-deepmind organization avatar.

records.title: Genie 3 / Project Genie
records.description: Generates interactive video worlds from prompts for real-time exploration.

blocks.value: Generates interactive video worlds from prompts for real-time exploration.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Google DeepMind's August 2025 research demonstration reported interactive worlds at 720p and 24 FPS with consistency lasting several minutes. The separate Project Genie prototype limits exploration to 60 seconds; its current help page requires an eligible personal Google AI Ultra account, age 18+, where Ultra is available. Video download is documented, while downloadable engine source, exportable level assets, and deterministic gameplay rules are not established by these sources.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: Genie 3 is introduced on the official Google DeepMind blog. Use the official google-deepmind organization avatar, consistently with the original Genie paper.

records.title: GameNGen — Diffusion Models Are Real-Time Game Engines
records.description: Trains an interactive diffusion simulator from DOOM gameplay trajectories.

blocks.value: GameNGen — Diffusion Models Are Real-Time Game Engines
Trains an interactive diffusion simulator from DOOM gameplay trajectories.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: A reinforcement learning agent first collects game trajectories. A diffusion model then predicts the next frame from visual history and actions, using conditioning noise augmentation to reduce autoregressive error. The paper demonstrates real-time DOOM simulation on a single TPU. This game-specific neural simulation does not automatically provide maintainable general game rules or an asset pipeline.

records.title: DIAMOND — Diffusion for World Modeling
records.description: Trains reinforcement learning agents inside diffusion world models that preserve visual detail.

blocks.value: Trains reinforcement learning agents inside diffusion world models that preserve visual detail.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Visual Details Matter in Atari studies diffusion models as environment models in which agents learn from imagined trajectories, analyzing how visual detail affects policies. Alongside the Atari 100k evaluation, the paper trains a playable neural engine on prerecorded CS:GO gameplay. It is relevant to simulation, control, and accumulated prediction error.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: The project page lists equal-contribution first authors Eloi Alonso (University of Geneva) and Adam Jelley (University of Edinburgh), with Microsoft Research also involved. Select the first author’s first institution, Geneva. The SVG is from the official university homepage and was provided/verified by the root agent.

records.title: GameFactory
records.description: Combines open-domain video generation with keyboard and mouse action control.

blocks.value: Combines open-domain video generation with keyboard and mouse action control.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Creating New Games with Generative Interactive Videos proposes domain adapters and action-control modules for autoregressive game video. The public GF-Minecraft dataset includes action labels; the checked repository provides dataset documentation and detection/visualization utilities, without establishing a released training/inference pipeline or model weights. Visual generalization should be evaluated separately from rule correctness, item persistence, and exportable game projects.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution

records.title: Oasis: A Universe in a Transformer
records.description: A neural game research release that predicts Minecraft-style frames from prior frames and actions.

blocks.value: Oasis: A Universe in a Transformer
A neural game research release that predicts Minecraft-style frames from prior frames and actions.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Oasis by Decart and Etched uses a Transformer autoencoder and latent diffusion. Its MIT-licensed inference code and 500M checkpoint are a downsized release, separate from the larger hosted demo. Hugging Face currently gates weight downloads behind agreement to share contact information. The public script generates video from an initial frame and action sequence; it does not establish a complete live game interface or training pipeline. The authors identify limits in long-term memory, precise inventory control, generalization, and object consistency.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: The official Oasis page credits Decart and Etched and specifically credits the AI team at Decart. Select the model team’s company, Decart, while acknowledging Etched. The logo is the footer image explicitly labeled Decart signet in https://decart.ai/ HTML.

records.title: WonderWorld
records.description: Builds an explorable, expandable explicit 3D scene from a single image.

blocks.value: Builds an explorable, expandable explicit 3D scene from a single image.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Interactive 3D Scene Generation from a Single Image uses Fast Layered Gaussian Surfels and guided depth diffusion to connect new scenes as the camera moves and prompts change. It provides explicit spatial representation and real-time rendering, primarily addressing geometry and appearance. Interactive gameplay, physics, and persistent dynamic state still require separate implementation.

blocks.label: Identity & attribution
blocks.value: The author page lists equal-contribution first authors Hong-Xing (Koven) Yu and Haoyi Duan at Stanford University, with MIT also represented. Select Stanford. The logo is the official touch icon linked by https://identity.stanford.edu/.

records.title: World Labs Marble
records.description: Generates persistent, navigable 3D scenes with splat and mesh exports.

blocks.value: Generates persistent, navigable 3D scenes with splat and mesh exports.

blocks.label: Why it belongs here
blocks.value: Marble supports multimodal world creation, exports Gaussian splats, visual meshes, and collision meshes for approximate physics, and renders video along camera paths. Compared with pure video continuation, it produces spatial assets for downstream engines. Developers still need to build character behavior, quest logic, and game loops. According to the inspected web-app guide, collider mesh export is included with Standard and high-quality textured GLB export requires Pro.

blocks.label: AI workflow / foundation context
blocks.value: The creator identifies Claude Code, GitHub Copilot, GPT Image 2, PixelLab and Meshy among the production tools. The repository documents Meshy rigs and animation, Blender retargeting and PixelOver sprite exports. The exact coding models and division of code between assistants are not specified; generated NPC teammates are not the evidence for AI-assisted development.

blocks.label: Study this workflow
items: Open the itch prototype and choose one human player, then claim a keyboard and select a costume.
Read the creator’s AI disclosure and the repository’s character, combat and sprite-pipeline notes.
Open project.godot in Godot 4.7 using GL Compatibility; the finished sprites and game scenes are included.
Change one combat or spawn setting, then check the title-to-character-to-dungeon flow, damage and restart.

items.label: Read the game and asset-pipeline documentation
Play Katana Kitsune on itch.io
items.note: Silent HTML5 prototype with keyboard and gamepad support. Space confirms player/device choices; allow a clear press and release between setup steps. The browser build loaded and reached player/device selection in review; combat and a complete dungeon run were not exercised. The download is large: about 184 MB of game data plus 40 MB of WebAssembly.

items.label: Open the complete Godot game project
items.note: Godot 4.7 project with scenes, GDScript, Dialogic addon and finished sprite assets. The inspected tree contains about 383 MB of files; no top-level game license was found. The upstream Meshy/Blender/PixelOver authoring pipeline is separate, while its finished runtime sprites are committed. The current source contains newer party/asset changes than the reviewed hosted prototype.

items.label: Read the creator’s AI production disclosure
items.note: The author explicitly names Claude Code and GitHub Copilot alongside image, sprite and 3D asset tools, and links the primary complete source repository. The README verifies the Godot version and explains which finished assets are included.

records.description: Guide a rising performer through a year of career choices in a card-based fame simulation. Play cards to build craft, money and attention while three newspapers react and excessive heat turns into scandals.

blocks.value: Guide a rising performer through a year of career choices in a card-based fame simulation. Play cards to build craft, money and attention while three newspapers react and excessive heat turns into scandals.

Use Node.js 22.18+ with npm install and npm run dev; trace content/cards.json through core/reducer.ts and the React desk before testing a complete year.

records.description: Slide across icy 3D arenas, use a three-hit melee combo to propel yourself forward, and fire projectiles that push you backward. Open gates and collect coins while confronting a rat regime in a short game-jam adventure.

blocks.value: Slide across icy 3D arenas, use a three-hit melee combo to propel yourself forward, and fire projectiles that push you backward. Open gates and collect coins while confronting a rat regime in a short game-jam adventure.

blocks.label: AI workflow / foundation context
blocks.value: Aidan “Botodo” Connolly and Evan Kurtz describe Claude Code helping diagnose problems and implement difficult core logic; they then touched and tweaked all code. They modeled, rigged, animated and designed the game themselves, using credited external audio. They explicitly state that generative AI was not used to create assets. No coding model version is supplied.

items: Start the first browser level with a mouse and test the slippery movement and melee combo.

Open the slick project folder in Godot 4.6, change one movement or gate rule, and test the first room, ammo and pause/restart controls.

items.label: Read the team’s development and asset breakdown

items.note: Mouse recommended: left-click performs melee propulsion, right-click shoots with recoil, and Escape pauses. Browser review reached the first level, moved, fired a projectile with ammo changing from 12 to 11, and opened pause. The roughly 170 MB web build has author-documented performance limits; Windows/Linux downloads are provided and mobile is not recommended. Later levels and a complete run were not tested.

items.label: Open the complete Godot game project
items.note: Complete Godot 4.6 project with levels, GDScript, GLB/FBX models, Blender authoring files, textures, UI and audio. The inspected tree has 292 files, about 239 MB. Open the slick folder; importing Blender authoring files may require a compatible Blender installation. No top-level game license was found; external sounds, music and fonts retain their separately credited terms.

items.label: Read the team’s explicit Claude Code assistance statement
items.note: The creators distinguish AI help with diagnosing and implementing core code from their own code review, modeling, animation and art. blocks.value: Cloud Crush: Gemini CLI builds a match-3 game
Match cloud-service icons on an eight-by-eight board, chase a timed high score, and create special Gemini gems. Google publishes the complete Go game alongside a detailed Gemini CLI codelab.

blocks.label: AI workflow / foundation context

blocks.label: Study this workflow
items: Download the devrel-demos repository and enter codelabs/gemini-cli/gemini-cli-match3-golang. Install Go 1.26.2 or newer; the README’s 1.24+ prerequisite is outdated. For native desktop play, run: go run .

Follow the title and player-name prompts. Use arrow keys to move the cursor and Space to select a gem, then an arrow to swap. Mouse/touch input is also implemented. Compare matching, falling tiles, time bonuses, and score behavior with main.go.

For a local browser build, first prepare the files served by the Go server: mkdir -p public/assets; cp assets/* public/assets/; cp index.html public/index.html. The committed public/assets directory is missing source files required by the game, including background.jpg.

Use the WASM helper from the same Go installation as the compiler: cp "$(go env GOROOT)/lib/wasm/wasm_exec.js" public/wasm_exec.js. Then compile: GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm go build -o public/cloud-crush.wasm .

Run the browser server from the same game directory: go run server/main.go. Open http://localhost:8080. Local play does not require Gemini CLI, an API key, a Google Cloud account, or cloud deployment.

Read the official codelab to trace the development prompts. The browser instructions above were checked against source; this review did not install Go or compile the game. Its preview is a publisher-provided gameplay screenshot.

blocks.value: Small, separate engine projects for character control, physics, navigation, networking, animation and import/export regression tests.

items.label: Play browser demos
items.note: Free browser builds and downloadable source projects. Browser exports cover a subset of the repository.

blocks.label: Code license
blocks.value: MIT; retain the repository license and notices.

blocks.label: Asset license
blocks.value: Repository MIT license applies unless an individual demo or bundled resource states otherwise; keep local attribution notices.

blocks.label: AI use and evaluation boundary
blocks.value: A useful open-license baseline for code editing and automated playtests. Record licenses of any additional assets or plugins rather than treating the demo license as a grant for unrelated data.

blocks.label: Try these tasks
items: Change one movement or collision rule and verify the original scene still starts and completes its objective.
Import a known model or animation, then compare material loading, scale, skeleton mapping and exported behavior.
Replay the same input sequence and record screenshots, errors and task completion.

blocks.label: Setup
items: Choose a stable demo branch or release compatible with the installed Godot version; pin its commit.
Download one demo directory, import its project.godot and run its main scene.
Save the engine version, scene, input sequence and expected result alongside the baseline.

blocks.label: Limitations
blocks.value: Not installed or run in this research pass. Hosted web demos redeploy from master on every commit, so their URLs are not immutable baselines. Pin a compatible source commit for repeatable tests; the development branch and web renderer can differ from stable desktop behavior.

records.title: SuperTux
records.description: A complete platform game for jump timing, collision, level editing and visual/input regression tasks in a substantial native codebase.

blocks.value: A complete platform game for jump timing, collision, level editing and visual/input regression tasks in a substantial native codebase.

items.label: Play official browser build
items.note: Official browser play, a free Steam release and independent desktop downloads are available. Building modified core code requires the native toolchain.

blocks.label: Code license
blocks.value: GNU GPL; inspect the pinned version and component notices before distributing a modified build.

blocks.label: Asset license
blocks.value: Most game data uses CC BY-SA; individual files and third-party components have additional notices.

blocks.label: AI use and evaluation boundary
blocks.value: Code access supports instrumented experiments, but GPL code and CC BY-SA game data carry different obligations. Keep any redistributed screenshots, maps or data exports traceable to their source licenses.

blocks.label: Try these tasks
items: Modify jump acceleration or a collision edge case, then replay a fixed level.
Measure completion rate, deaths, missed jumps and time for a screen-based controller.
Change a level and verify checkpoints, enemies and completion conditions.

blocks.label: Setup
items: Start with the free binary and a fixed level to establish a control baseline.
For code edits, follow the repository build instructions with CMake and the required C++ dependencies.
Pin the game version, level, settings and input timing before comparing agents.

blocks.label: Limitations
blocks.value: Not installed or run in this research pass. It has no ready-made Gymnasium evaluation contract; observation, action timing and reset/success detection need a harness.

records.title: Crafter
records.description: A compact survival world combining exploration, health, gathering, construction and crafting. Achievement progress exposes different strengths of a playing agent.

blocks.value: A compact survival world combining exploration, health, gathering, construction and crafting. Achievement progress exposes different strengths of a playing agent.

blocks.label: Asset license
blocks.value: Repository material under its MIT notice; track any replacement art separately.

items.label: Pinned reset, seed and privileged info contract

blocks.label: AI use and evaluation boundary
blocks.value: Designed for agent evaluation. For pixel-only tests, withhold info.semantic, inventory and player_pos from the policy; those expose structured state beyond the RGB observation. Keep published benchmark budgets separate from custom VLM protocols.

items: Measure survival and achievement success over held-out world seeds.

items: Install crafter and pygame in an isolated Python environment.
Run python -m crafter.run_gui for manual controls, then use CrafterReward-v1 for automation.

Set the seed when constructing the environment and record the episode index; use crafter.Recorder with a nonempty output directory, save_stats=True and save_episode=True to retain completed-episode statistics and action trajectories.

blocks.label: Limitations
blocks.value: Source reviewed, not run here. Classic Gym reset returns only an observation and step returns four values. reset has no seed argument; matching constructor seeds alone is insufficient unless episode/reset order also matches.

records.title: Craftax

items: Compare survival and crafting progress using identical seeded worlds.

blocks.label: Limitations
blocks.value: Source reviewed, not run here. JIT startup is slow. With auto_reset=True, a done step returns the next episode observation/state alongside the previous episode reward/done/info. With auto_reset=False, handle termination before stepping again.
